17 November 2026, 10am-12pm, room Salle 70, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Site François-Mitterrand.
Malametenia Vlachou-Efstathiou (IRHT/IMAGINE-ENPC)
Title: Computational Modelling of Medieval Handwriting for Task-Agnostic Paleographical Analysis
Abstract: How can computational methods support the description and comparison of medieval handwriting beyond specific classification tasks? This presentation introduces a computer-vision framework for the quantitative and interpretable characterization of historical scripts, combining character morphology with the measurement of spatial properties. Starting from text-line images and their transcriptions, the method detects character instances without requiring manual character-level annotations and produces visual prototypes of letterforms alongside metrological descriptors capturing their dimensions and position within the line.
The presentation examines the technical and methodological choices underlying these representations and their implications for paleographical research. Through different case studies, it aims to show how such an approach can help identify shared and discriminative features, reassess relationships between scribal hands, and investigate the consistency and variability of writing practices. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between computational representations and paleographical interpretation, and to how quantitative measurements and visual evidence can complement established methods of handwriting analysis.
